statements.text: So, data is a place to start, because what feeds AI? Lots and lots of data, and we should make sure that we're protecting data as the first place to start.
statements.venue: TV interview transcript, 'DelBene on Regulating AI: Privacy is the Fundamental Building Block'

statements.text: But before we build the second and third story of this regulatory house, we need to lay a strong foundation and that must center around a national data privacy standard.
statements.venue: Newsweek op-ed by Suzan K. DelBene

statements.text: AI developers do not need to disclose where they get their input data from because the U.S. has no national privacy law.
statements.venue: Newsweek op-ed by Suzan K. DelBene

statements.text: If we want a seat at the international table to set the long-term direction for AI that reflects our core American values, we must have our own national data privacy law to start.
statements.venue: Newsweek op-ed by Suzan K. DelBene

statements.text:
AI is trained on huge amounts of data - potentially your chats, posts, & other info because we don't have a national privacy law.

The most important first step Congress can take to put guardrails around AI & protect Americans is a national privacy law.

https://t.co/cFQR0A79kZ

Joined Bloomberg's Sound On to discuss the future of AI and the urgent need to pass federal privacy legislation that protects our personal information from unknowingly being used to train AI products. https://t.co/5oDviJM7xZ

With AI in the spotlight, we cannot lose sight of why we need a strong national data privacy law that puts people back in control of their info.

Privacy protections go beyond AI & help keep us safe online, on our phones, & even in our smart cars.

As lawmakers discuss the right way put guardrails around emerging AI tools, strong federal data protection must be a key component.

I am working in Congress to pass a national data privacy law that gives you control over your data.

Listen & read more ⬇️.
https://t.co/L7LCMgSno9

I welcome @POTUS’ executive action to promote the safe use of AI. But to make lasting change & ensure the U.S. is leading the way globally, Congress must pass privacy legislation that protects people & their data. I will continue working with my colleagues to get this done. https://t.co/4t2rHTcHZ4
statements.quoted:
Artificial Intelligence is moving quickly.

And so is my Administration.

Visit https://t.co/RqhfxoxjQ6 and see how we're harnessing the power of AI and keeping all Americans safe in the process.

statements.text: The United States must be in the driver's seat as artificial intelligence expands around the world and President Biden clearly understands that. I welcome the president's executive order to ensure AI is implemented in a safe and secure way, especially his focus on consumer privacy protections.
statements.venue: DelBene press release responding to Biden AI executive order

statements.text:
AI is creating more realistic deepfakes, making it harder to tell the difference between what’s real & what’s fake. @RepBuddyCarter & I joined @ASP to discuss how this technology can be abused & what Congress can do to set strong guardrails.

Watch here ⬇️
https://t.co/3FcR3meq6B

As AI evolves, Congress must set strong guardrails to prevent abuse by passing forward-looking protections.

I’ve been leading the effort to pass a national data privacy law that keeps our sensitive data safe & holds violators accountable.

As this technology is updated, I wondered if you could speak about how emerging technologies like artificial intelligence are being integrated into the IRS's work to provide services to taxpayers and to enforce tax laws. And how is the IRS addressing data privacy and security concerns inherent with such technologies?
statements.context: Exchange during a House hearing where Representative Suzan DelBene asks Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen about AI integration at the IRS.

statements.text:

Beginning in January, private companies will start using AI to review certain health care services, potentially delaying or denying Medicare beneficiaries from getting the care they’ve earned.

I introduced legislation to stop this program. Health decisions should be made between patients & their doctors, not profit-driven algorithms.

This program, known as the Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) program, pays private companies to use AI to review Medicare claims.
statements.venue: Op-ed by Rep. DelBene: Trump's AI experiment is coming for seniors' cancer treatments

statements.text: When Democrats take control of the House in November, we need to rigorously investigate this program so more seniors like Joanne aren't victims of this reckless AI experiment.

statements.text: Under WISeR, outside companies are paid a share of the costs they “save” by rejecting claims. This creates a pervasive incentive to deny care.
